designs.assertions:
What breaks if the AP path regresses — every one of these was run and observed, not predicted:

1. detect_variant() stops returning "red_ap"/"blue_ap". The gate FAILS on `detect_variant() reports the AP build as such` whenever the seed-slot verdict and the reported variant disagree. This is the regression that matters most because in production it is SILENT: the client falls back to `red`, binds vanilla addresses, and a Soul Link run reads the wrong byte for its current map, badges, trainer ID, PC box and enemy party while looking perfectly healthy. It has already happened once (the old CPU-0xFFDB read made every vanilla cart eventually self-identify as AP).

2. BizHawk stops exposing a flat "ROM" domain, or exposes a 32 KB bus window instead. FAILS `BizHawk exposes a flat 'ROM' domain` / `the ROM domain is the whole 1 MB cartridge`. detect_archipelago() is built entirely on that domain; nothing else in the repo touches it.

3. Archipelago ships a pokemon_rb whose fork moved WRAM again, without data/pret_syms.json being rebuilt. FAILS `the ROM's own code agrees with the seed slot about which build this is` (the seed slot still says AP, bank 0 no longer references 0xD436) AND every `initProfile bound <FIELD>` for the fields that moved. This is the provenance check — the only thing anywhere connecting the symbol table to the ROM a player actually loads.

4. Someone deletes an override from the red_ap block, or adds a field to `red` that red_ap must not inherit. The metatable inheritance means a missing override reads as a plausible vanilla address, not as nil. FAILS the specific `initProfile bound <FIELD>` line with `got 0xD35E, want 0xD436`. Thirteen fields are pinned.

5. Someone "fixes" AP by shifting everything uniformly. FAILS `initProfile left wPartyCount where the fork leaves it` / `... wIsInBattle ...`. The fork moves 16 of 45 fields and leaves 28 alone; a blanket delta is wrong in both directions.

6. The memorial-box SRAM guard drifts off wCurrentBoxNum. FAILS `the memorial SRAM guard points at the bound wCurrentBoxNum`. wCurrentBoxNum moves +116 in the fork, further than the rest of the box block; writing BIT_HAS_CHANGED_BOXES at vanilla 0xD5A0 on an AP cartridge sets bit 7 of an unrelated byte, ChangeBox's `call z, EmptyAllSRAMBoxes` is then taken, and the memorial is wiped with no error anywhere.

7. rom_type_for_variant() reverts to a display label ("Red (AP)"). FAILS `rom_type_for_variant() returns a server-side KEY`. That string is fed to _ROM_TYPE_TO_GAME_ID; a label binds game_id=None and the hello never attaches an adapter.

8. The AP ROM stops booting, or a future apworld option skips the intro. FAILS `the cartridge boots and the game writes the BOUND wCurMap`, with a screenshot at patch/build/test_gen1_ap_gate_bootfail.png. This is what stops checks 1-7 from passing on a ROM that is merely a well-formed brick.

9. The gate stops proving anything. FAILS `the operand scan works at all` (the positive control, wIsInBattle, must be referenced in bank 0) or `bank 0 references exactly one of the two wCurMap addresses` or `the OTHER build's wCurMap is not also reading a bedroom`. These three exist so the gate cannot go green by measuring nothing.

Note the pairing: `--rom red_ap` and `--rom red_cold` run the SAME file and every AP assertion has to come out the other way. A detection function stuck at "yes" passes the first and fails the second; stuck at "no", vice versa. Neither run alone is worth much — pytest parametrizes all four (red_ap, blue_ap, red_cold, blue_cold) so they cannot be separated.
designs.risks:
HOW THIS COULD PASS WHILE BROKEN
* It never touches a live party, box, or write path. Reads (readPartySlot, readBoxSlot, key derivation), writes (forceFaint, depositPartyMon, writeEnemyParty, depositMemorialMon), the deferred-command queue and the server handshake are UNPROVEN on AP. They are the same profile-driven code vanilla proves on three cartridges, and the addresses they use are now confirmed, but "the address is right" is not "the struct read at that base is right". Closing that needs the fixture (below).
* The bank-0 operand scan is a byte-pattern search, not a disassembler: an `FA 36 D4` that is actually data would count. Mitigated by the margin (25 vs 0, and 72 vs 0 whole-ROM) and by requiring exactly one of the two candidates to be nonzero — but a hostile coincidence at exactly the wrong address would not be caught.
* The liveness check pins one address (wCurMap) at one moment. The other twelve `initProfile bound` assertions are static comparisons against literals I derived from the same symbol table the profile uses — the ROM-code differential is what makes that non-circular, and it only covers wCurMap. A field that moved differently from what alchav's .sym says would pass.
* `t.variant:find("_ap")` accepts any variant containing "_ap"; it is a shape check, not an identity check. The `initProfile bound` block is what actually pins Red vs Blue behaviour, and Red and Blue share a layout, so a red/blue mix-up would not be caught here (the ROM title read in detect_variant is the only thing separating them).
* The apworld and the vanilla dumps are external and gitignored, so on any machine without them all four params SKIP — green by absence. Same posture as every other Gen 1 live gate, but worth saying out loud.

FLAKE
* Low. Three runs, three deterministic frame numbers: red_ap 688, red_cold 688, blue_ap 704. Nothing waits on a menu, a naming screen, a text box or an encounter — the failure modes that make gen1_playthrough.lua flaky are all downstream of where this stops. The 24000-frame budget is ~35x the observed 688.
* The one real dependency is that the intro still reaches map 0x26. Measured identical on vanilla and AP, which is itself evidence the fork does not touch the intro.
* Cold boot means BizHawk must not find a stale SaveRAM. The runner deletes it by name; if BizHawk ever changes how it derives a name from an unknown ROM hash, a stale save would put the title screen on CONTINUE and the gate would fail loudly (never became 0x26) rather than silently.

WHAT IS STILL NOT WORTH DOING, AND WHAT IT WOULD COST
The full fixture path — an AP battery save, after which test_gen1_memory_gate.lua and test_gen1_writes_gate.lua run UNCHANGED (their assertions are 100% profile-driven; the writes gate's ChangeBox ROM-byte check is already gated on `change_box_bit_test_rom_addr`, which is `false` for AP and therefore falsy-skipped in Lua). The mechanical cost is small and fully enumerated: the six A-table addresses plus two SRAM constants listed above, three registry lines (gen1_playthrough.py ROMS, run_gen1_gate.py SAVERAM_NAMES, tests/live ROMS). The unknown cost is iterating gen1_playthrough.lua's intro/START-menu drive against a ROM nobody has driven — historically the expensive part, and it is exactly the kind of work that eats an afternoon on flake rather than on logic. Two things now argue it would go easily: the intro is frame-identical to vanilla (688 on both), and the AP fork does not add a START-menu entry, so SAVE_INDEX = 3 should still hold. I would spend that afternoon only if someone actually intends to run an AP Soul Link. The gate above buys the part that fails SILENTLY for a fraction of the cost; the fixture buys the part that fails LOUDLY.
Duo E2E on AP: not worth it at any point I can foresee. It would re-test Soul Link rules against server code that never sees a WRAM address, at 2x emulator cost.
